end-to-end.question: Why did a king hold a sacrifice meant to burn all the snakes?
end-to-end.answer: King Janamejaya held the snake-sacrifice to avenge himself on the snake Takshaka, who had killed his father, King Parikshit [1]. He desired to burn Takshaka and his relatives in the fire just as his father had been burnt by the snake's poison [1].

correctness.reason: The answer correctly identifies that King Janamejaya held the sacrifice to avenge his father Parikshit, who was killed by Takshaka, and aimed to burn Takshaka and his relatives.

relevance.reason: The answer directly explains the reason why King Janamejaya performed the snake sacrifice.
